7. audit (phase 0; event log by 20 Nov, the rest by 27 Nov)

audit.events replaces activities as the one event log. It cannot be updated or deleted, and every Deal view History row, decision and send is an event.

-- rev 0015_audit
CREATE TABLE audit.events (                        -- append-only; no updated_at
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  event_type text NOT NULL CHECK (event_type ~ '^[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+$'),   -- e.g. mandate.stage_changed
  actor_kind text NOT NULL CHECK (actor_kind IN ('user','system','ai','attio')),
  actor_user_id uuid REFERENCES core.users ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  CHECK (actor_kind <> 'user' OR actor_user_id IS NOT NULL),
  mandate_id uuid REFERENCES core.mandates ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  counterparty_id uuid REFERENCES core.counterparties ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  organization_id uuid REFERENCES core.organizations ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  person_id uuid REFERENCES core.people ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  source text NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('engine','slack','mcp','attio','gmail','calendar','scribe','vantagekit','drive','system')),
  source_url text,                                  -- every History row links to its source (MH3)
  summary text NOT NULL,
  decision_reason text, CHECK (event_type <> 'decision.logged' OR decision_reason IS NOT NULL),
  idempotency_key text UNIQUE,
  correlation_id uuid,
  ledger_kind text, ledger_id uuid,                 -- pointer to a module run ledger (tool_runs, command_runs)
  detail jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',              -- typed per event_type, validated by Pydantic
  raw_input_id uuid);                               -- the input that caused it; FK added below
CREATE INDEX ix_events_mandate_time ON audit.events (mandate_id, occurred_at DESC) WHERE mandate_id IS NOT NULL;   -- History tab
CREATE INDEX ix_events_cp_time ON audit.events (counterparty_id, occurred_at DESC) WHERE counterparty_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_events_org_time ON audit.events (organization_id, occurred_at DESC) WHERE organization_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_events_person ON audit.events (person_id) WHERE person_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_events_actor ON audit.events (actor_user_id) WHERE actor_user_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_events_type_time ON audit.events (event_type, occurred_at DESC);      -- firm feed, what changed
CREATE INDEX ix_events_correlation ON audit.events (correlation_id) WHERE correlation_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_events_brin ON audit.events USING brin (occurred_at);

CREATE FUNCTION util.forbid_change() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN RAISE EXCEPTION '% is append-only', TG_TABLE_NAME; END $$;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_events_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON audit.events
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION util.forbid_change();
-- Same trigger on comms.email_messages, comms.touchpoints, comms.classifier_feedback,
-- usage.ledger, work.notifications, work.notification_actions,
-- docs.skill_versions, dataroom.activity, audit.record_changes and audit.raw_inputs.

-- Field-level before and after for every UPDATE of a record. The API opens each write with
-- SET LOCAL wusool.event_id = '<the audit.events id it just wrote>'; an update without one is refused,
-- so no record can change without an event explaining who and why.
CREATE TABLE audit.record_changes (                 -- append-only
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  event_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.events ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  table_name text NOT NULL CHECK (table_name ~ '^[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+$'),
  record_id uuid NOT NULL,                         -- no FK: it spans many tables; the event carries the typed links
  field_code text NOT NULL,
  old_value text, new_value text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (event_id, table_name, record_id, field_code));
CREATE INDEX ix_record_changes_record ON audit.record_changes (table_name, record_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX ix_record_changes_field ON audit.record_changes (table_name, field_code, created_at DESC);

CREATE FUNCTION audit.capture_changes() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  ev uuid := nullif(current_setting('wusool.event_id', true), '')::uuid;
  o jsonb := to_jsonb(OLD); n jsonb := to_jsonb(NEW); k text;
BEGIN
  IF ev IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'update of %.% without an event (set wusool.event_id)', TG_TABLE_SCHEMA, TG_TABLE_NAME;
  END IF;
  FOR k IN SELECT jsonb_object_keys(n) LOOP
    CONTINUE WHEN k IN ('updated_at','updated_by','attio_synced_at');
    IF (o -> k) IS DISTINCT FROM (n -> k) THEN
      INSERT INTO audit.record_changes (event_id, table_name, record_id, field_code, old_value, new_value)
      VALUES (ev, TG_TABLE_SCHEMA || '.' || TG_TABLE_NAME,
              coalesce(n ->> 'id', n ->> 'mandate_id', n ->> 'partner_id')::uuid,   -- 1:1 tables key on their parent
              k, o ->> k, n ->> k);
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;
-- Attached AFTER UPDATE to every record table with an id: core.organizations, people, buyer_roles,
-- seller_roles, mandates, counterparties, prospect_lists, prospect_list_entries, notes; docs.materials,
-- offers, engagement_terms (by mandate_id); market.comps, vc_rounds, listed_comps, valuation_rules; firm.partners, partner_terms, scorecard_metrics;
-- work.approvals, tasks; outreach.drafts. Inserts are covered by their event; junction-table changes
-- (sectors, geographies, contacts) are written by the API as record_changes rows on the parent record.
-- CREATE TRIGGER trg_<table>_changes AFTER UPDATE ON <schema>.<table>
--   FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION audit.capture_changes();

CREATE TABLE audit.attio_field_map (               -- one row per live Attio attribute
  attio_parent text NOT NULL,                      -- organizations, person, deal, note, scorecards, buyer_role, ...
  attio_slug text NOT NULL,
  pg_table text NOT NULL, pg_column text,          -- NULL when the field maps to a junction table or view
  direction text NOT NULL CHECK (direction IN ('both','to_attio','from_attio','ignored')),
  note text,
  PRIMARY KEY (attio_parent, attio_slug));

-- Every input exactly as it arrived, kept forever and never changed (DFSA record-keeping).
CREATE TABLE audit.raw_inputs (                    -- append-only, kept forever
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  source text NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('attio_webhook','vantagekit_webhook','sanity_webhook','gmail_push','gmail_poll',
                                         'calendar_push','calendar_poll','lead_magnet','upload','claude_import','apollo',
                                         'scribe','bedrock','google_places','firecrawl')),
  external_id text,                                 -- the sender's event or message id
  received_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  content_type text NOT NULL,                       -- e.g. application/json, text/csv, application/pdf
  body bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(body) <= 52428800),   -- exact bytes, 50 MB cap
  sha256 char(64) NOT NULL CHECK (sha256 ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'),
  UNIQUE (source, external_id));
-- Readable JSON for ad-hoc queries, without ever storing a re-encoded copy.
CREATE VIEW audit.v_raw_json AS
  SELECT id, source, external_id, received_at, convert_from(body, 'UTF8')::jsonb AS json
  FROM audit.raw_inputs WHERE content_type = 'application/json';

-- One cited passage of a raw input. Every value from an outside source and every AI-written
-- sentence the web shows points at one or more of these. Append-only.
CREATE TABLE audit.evidence (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  raw_input_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.raw_inputs ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  locator_kind text NOT NULL CHECK (locator_kind IN ('whole','json_path','char_range','row','page','transcript_segments')),
  locator text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',                 -- '$.data.revenue' | '1203-1388' | '42' | '3' | 'seg_12-seg_15'
  CHECK ((locator_kind = 'whole') = (locator = '')),
  quote text CHECK (length(quote) <= 2000),         -- the passage as shown on the source chip
  url text,                                         -- where it was published, when there is one
  captured_at timestamptz NOT NULL,                 -- when we fetched it
  cited_by text NOT NULL CHECK (cited_by IN ('ai','system','user')));
CREATE INDEX ix_evidence_raw ON audit.evidence (raw_input_id);
CREATE TRIGGER trg_evidence_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON audit.evidence
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION util.forbid_change();

-- Single-source claims: one evidence link each.
ALTER TABLE intake.field_sources ADD COLUMN evidence_id uuid REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  ADD CONSTRAINT ck_field_sources_evidence CHECK (source IN ('user','attio') OR evidence_id IS NOT NULL);
ALTER TABLE intake.field_proposals ADD COLUMN evidence_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT;
ALTER TABLE work.approvals ADD COLUMN evidence_id uuid REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  ADD CONSTRAINT ck_approvals_evidence CHECK (source = 'rule' OR evidence_id IS NOT NULL);
ALTER TABLE market.comps ADD COLUMN evidence_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT;   -- the dataset row or the saved web page
ALTER TABLE market.web_comp_results ADD COLUMN evidence_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT;
ALTER TABLE market.vc_rounds ADD COLUMN evidence_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT;
ALTER TABLE market.listed_comps ADD COLUMN evidence_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT;
ALTER TABLE market.valuation_rules ADD COLUMN evidence_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT;   -- seeded rows point into the uploaded valuation.json; Claude edits point at the call
CREATE INDEX ix_field_sources_evidence ON intake.field_sources (evidence_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_field_proposals_evidence ON intake.field_proposals (evidence_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_approvals_evidence ON work.approvals (evidence_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_comps_evidence ON market.comps (evidence_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_web_comps_evidence ON market.web_comp_results (evidence_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_vc_rounds_evidence ON market.vc_rounds (evidence_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_listed_comps_evidence ON market.listed_comps (evidence_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_rules_evidence ON market.valuation_rules (evidence_id);
-- The kept enrichment tables (intake.signals, intake.linkedin_scans) gain the same
-- evidence_id NOT NULL column in the cutover revision that moves them.

-- Multi-source claims: one row per sentence or line and the passages behind it.
CREATE TABLE core.mandate_blurb_citations (
  blurb_id uuid REFERENCES core.mandate_blurbs ON DELETE CASCADE,
  sentence_no smallint CHECK (sentence_no >= 1),
  evidence_id uuid REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  PRIMARY KEY (blurb_id, sentence_no, evidence_id));
CREATE INDEX ix_blurb_citations_evidence ON core.mandate_blurb_citations (evidence_id);

CREATE TABLE work.daily_brief_item_citations (
  brief_id uuid, position smallint,
  evidence_id uuid REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  PRIMARY KEY (brief_id, position, evidence_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (brief_id, position) REFERENCES work.daily_brief_items ON DELETE CASCADE);
CREATE INDEX ix_brief_citations_evidence ON work.daily_brief_item_citations (evidence_id);

CREATE TABLE comms.meeting_summary_item_citations (  -- transcript lines behind each point
  summary_item_id uuid REFERENCES comms.meeting_summary_items ON DELETE CASCADE,
  evidence_id uuid REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  PRIMARY KEY (summary_item_id, evidence_id));
CREATE INDEX ix_summary_citations_evidence ON comms.meeting_summary_item_citations (evidence_id);

CREATE TABLE intake.search_candidate_citations (     -- the records and pages behind "why this match"
  candidate_id uuid REFERENCES intake.search_candidates ON DELETE CASCADE,
  evidence_id uuid REFERENCES audit.evidence ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  PRIMARY KEY (candidate_id, evidence_id));
CREATE INDEX ix_candidate_citations_evidence ON intake.search_candidate_citations (evidence_id);

-- "No citation, no claim", checked at commit so a claim and its citations can be written in any order.
CREATE FUNCTION util.require_citation() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'mandate_blurbs' AND NEW.status = 'approved'
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core.mandate_blurb_citations WHERE blurb_id = NEW.id) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'approved blurb % has no citations', NEW.id;
  ELSIF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'daily_brief_items'
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM work.daily_brief_item_citations WHERE brief_id = NEW.brief_id AND position = NEW.position) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'brief line %/% has no citations', NEW.brief_id, NEW.position;
  ELSIF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'meeting_summary_items' AND NEW.kind IN ('decision','action_item','claim_to_verify','risk')
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comms.meeting_summary_item_citations WHERE summary_item_id = NEW.id) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'summary item % has no transcript citation', NEW.id;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;
CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER trg_blurbs_cited AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON core.mandate_blurbs
  DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION util.require_citation();
CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER trg_brief_items_cited AFTER INSERT ON work.daily_brief_items
  DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION util.require_citation();
CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER trg_summary_items_cited AFTER INSERT ON comms.meeting_summary_items
  DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION util.require_citation();

-- What the web's source chip reads (GET /api/v1/evidence/{id}).
CREATE VIEW audit.v_evidence_card AS
  SELECT e.id, e.quote, e.url, e.captured_at, e.locator_kind, e.locator, e.cited_by,
         r.source, r.content_type, r.received_at, r.id AS raw_input_id
  FROM audit.evidence e JOIN audit.raw_inputs r ON r.id = e.raw_input_id;
CREATE INDEX ix_raw_inputs_source_time ON audit.raw_inputs (source, received_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX ix_raw_inputs_brin ON audit.raw_inputs USING brin (received_at);

CREATE TABLE audit.raw_input_processing (          -- the only mutable part: how processing went
  raw_input_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES audit.raw_inputs ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  handler text NOT NULL,                            -- e.g. attio.webhook, gmail.push, vantagekit.event
  handler_version text NOT NULL,                    -- bumped when the handler's logic changes
  processed_at timestamptz, attempts smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, last_error text);
CREATE INDEX ix_raw_processing_pending ON audit.raw_input_processing (raw_input_id) WHERE processed_at IS NULL;
-- Replay: find inputs a fixed handler has not re-run yet.
CREATE INDEX ix_raw_processing_handler ON audit.raw_input_processing (handler, handler_version);

-- Link the records built from raw inputs back to them.
ALTER TABLE intake.import_batches ADD COLUMN raw_input_id uuid REFERENCES audit.raw_inputs ON DELETE RESTRICT;
ALTER TABLE intake.lead_submissions ADD COLUMN raw_input_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.raw_inputs ON DELETE RESTRICT;
ALTER TABLE comms.meetings ADD COLUMN raw_input_id uuid REFERENCES audit.raw_inputs ON DELETE RESTRICT;
CREATE INDEX ix_import_batches_raw ON intake.import_batches (raw_input_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_lead_submissions_raw ON intake.lead_submissions (raw_input_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_meetings_raw ON comms.meetings (raw_input_id);
ALTER TABLE comms.email_messages ADD CONSTRAINT fk_messages_raw FOREIGN KEY (raw_input_id) REFERENCES audit.raw_inputs ON DELETE RESTRICT;
CREATE INDEX ix_messages_raw ON comms.email_messages (raw_input_id);
ALTER TABLE usage.ledger ADD CONSTRAINT fk_ledger_raw FOREIGN KEY (raw_input_id) REFERENCES audit.raw_inputs ON DELETE RESTRICT;
ALTER TABLE intake.import_batches ADD CONSTRAINT ck_import_batches_raw CHECK (source = 'manual' OR raw_input_id IS NOT NULL);
ALTER TABLE docs.offer_extractions ADD CONSTRAINT fk_offer_extractions_raw FOREIGN KEY (raw_input_id) REFERENCES audit.raw_inputs ON DELETE RESTRICT;
CREATE INDEX ix_offer_extractions_raw ON docs.offer_extractions (raw_input_id);
ALTER TABLE audit.events ADD CONSTRAINT fk_events_raw_input FOREIGN KEY (raw_input_id) REFERENCES audit.raw_inputs ON DELETE RESTRICT;
CREATE INDEX ix_events_raw_input ON audit.events (raw_input_id) WHERE raw_input_id IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE audit.attio_sync_state (
  stream text PRIMARY KEY,                          -- e.g. organizations, deal, buyer_role
  cursor text, last_full_resync_at timestamptz, last_success_at timestamptz, last_error text);

CREATE TABLE audit.sessions (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES core.users ON DELETE CASCADE,
  expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL, revoked_at timestamptz,
  ip inet, user_agent text);
CREATE INDEX ix_sessions_user ON audit.sessions (user_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_sessions_expiry ON audit.sessions (expires_at) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE audit.idempotency_keys (               -- purged after 7 days
  key text PRIMARY KEY, scope text NOT NULL,
  response_status smallint, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now());
CREATE INDEX ix_idempotency_created ON audit.idempotency_keys (created_at);

CREATE TABLE audit.rate_limits (
  bucket text PRIMARY KEY, window_start timestamptz NOT NULL,
  hits integer NOT NULL CHECK (hits >= 0));

-- MCP sign-in (OAuth 2.1 per the MCP authorization spec). Tokens are kept only as SHA-256 hashes.
CREATE TABLE audit.oauth_clients (                  -- dynamic client registration, e.g. Claude
  client_id text PRIMARY KEY,
  client_name text NOT NULL,
  redirect_uris text[] NOT NULL CHECK (cardinality(redirect_uris) BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  revoked_at timestamptz);

CREATE TABLE audit.oauth_tokens (
  token_hash char(64) PRIMARY KEY CHECK (token_hash ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'),
  kind text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('authorization_code','access','refresh')),
  client_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES audit.oauth_clients ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES core.users ON DELETE CASCADE,
  scopes text[] NOT NULL,
  resource text NOT NULL,                           -- the /mcp address the token is bound to
  redirect_uri text, code_challenge text,           -- authorization codes only (PKCE S256)
  CHECK ((kind = 'authorization_code') = (code_challenge IS NOT NULL AND redirect_uri IS NOT NULL)),
  expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL, revoked_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now());
CREATE INDEX ix_oauth_tokens_user ON audit.oauth_tokens (user_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;   -- revoke on leave
CREATE INDEX ix_oauth_tokens_client ON audit.oauth_tokens (client_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_oauth_tokens_expiry ON audit.oauth_tokens (expires_at);   -- daily pg_cron purge

What happens to today's tables. Nothing is thrown away: each one carries on, moves into its module's schema, or has its data copied into its successor before it retires.

Today (public)In the new databaseHow
activitiesaudit.eventsEvery row copied, keeping its time, actor, subject and payload; activities retires after the copy is checked
deal_stage_eventscore.mandate_stage_history plus audit.eventsCopied through ref.attio_stage_map
tool_runsintake.tool_runs (kept)Moved and re-keyed; still the lead tools' run ledger, linked from events through ledger_kind/ledger_id; history feeds intake.lead_submissions
command_runsaudit.command_runs (kept)Moved and re-keyed; still the Slack command ledger
match_results, match_scoresintake (kept)Moved; *_attio_id columns become uuid keys to buyer and seller roles; each run links to an intake.search_runs row
discovery_reviews, linkedin_scans, signalsintake (kept)Moved and re-keyed to core
feedback_submissionscomms (kept)Moved
meetings, notescomms.meetings (+ transcripts, summary items), core.notesCopied; summary_json becomes summary item rows
interactions, interaction_participants, mailbox_sync_cursorscomms email, calendar and sync tablesCopied (all are empty today)
attio_raw_events, attio_sync_stateaudit.raw_inputs, audit.attio_sync_stateCopied; raw payloads are now kept forever
Mirror: organizations, person, deals, buyer_roles, seller_roles, userscoreBackfilled (Migration, step 4); renamed legacy_* after Attio retires, then dropped with a final snapshot
Unused drafts: buyer_intel, documents, graph_edges, scorecards, seller_financials, vertical_kb, investor_lender_roles–Dropped after a row count shows them empty

8. analytics (phase 0, by 4 Dec)

The numbers the dashboards and the weekly meeting read are precomputed in one schema, so reporting never scans the working tables during the day. Screens that must be live to the second (the Pipeline board, the Buyers tab rows, the stage bar) still read core through their indexes; summaries and trends read analytics.

-- rev 0016_analytics
CREATE SCHEMA analytics;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA analytics TO wusool_app, wusool_readonly;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE wusool_owner IN SCHEMA analytics GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO wusool_app, wusool_readonly;

-- Pipeline headline numbers (Home, weekly meeting, reporting).
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW analytics.pipeline_summary AS
SELECT m.owner_user_id, m.side, m.stage_code, m.status_code,
       count(*)                                                  AS mandates,
       sum(m.deal_value_usd)                                     AS deal_value_usd,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE m.next_step_due_on < current_date) AS next_step_overdue
FROM core.mandates m
WHERE m.removed_at IS NULL AND NOT m.is_test
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_pipeline_summary ON analytics.pipeline_summary (owner_user_id, side, stage_code, status_code);

-- Time in each stage, one row per visit (medians, conversion). The Deal view stage bar reads core.mandate_stage_history live instead, so it never lags the refresh.
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW analytics.stage_durations AS
SELECT h.id, h.mandate_id, m.side, h.stage_code, h.entered_at, h.left_at,
       extract(epoch FROM coalesce(h.left_at, now()) - h.entered_at) / 86400 AS days_in_stage
FROM core.mandate_stage_history h
JOIN core.mandates m ON m.id = h.mandate_id
WHERE m.removed_at IS NULL AND NOT m.is_test;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_stage_durations ON analytics.stage_durations (id);
CREATE INDEX ix_stage_durations_stage ON analytics.stage_durations (stage_code, entered_at) INCLUDE (days_in_stage);
CREATE INDEX ix_stage_durations_mandate ON analytics.stage_durations (mandate_id);

-- The deal-room funnel per mandate (PDF rules: cumulative; a view of the teaser or data room counts as opened).
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW analytics.mandate_funnel AS
SELECT c.mandate_id,
  count(*) AS counterparties,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comms.touchpoints t WHERE t.counterparty_id = c.id AND t.direction = 'outbound')) AS sent,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dataroom.links l JOIN dataroom.activity a ON a.link_id = l.id
                                 WHERE l.counterparty_id = c.id AND a.kind IN ('view','download'))) AS opened,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comms.touchpoints t WHERE t.counterparty_id = c.id AND t.direction = 'inbound')) AS replied,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.nda_signed_on IS NOT NULL) AS nda_signed,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comms.meetings mt WHERE mt.counterparty_id = c.id)) AS meeting_held,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM docs.offers o WHERE o.counterparty_id = c.id AND o.removed_at IS NULL)) AS ioi_received
FROM core.counterparties c
WHERE c.mandate_id IS NOT NULL AND c.removed_at IS NULL AND NOT c.is_test
GROUP BY c.mandate_id;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_mandate_funnel ON analytics.mandate_funnel (mandate_id);

-- Outreach reply rate by template and sector, last 90 days (Engine optimization, Outreach tiles).
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW analytics.reply_stats AS
SELECT t.template_code, m.sector_code,
       count(*) AS sent,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comms.touchpoints r
                                      WHERE r.counterparty_id = t.counterparty_id AND r.direction = 'inbound'
                                        AND r.occurred_at > t.occurred_at)) AS replied
FROM comms.touchpoints t
JOIN core.counterparties c ON c.id = t.counterparty_id
LEFT JOIN core.mandates m ON m.id = c.mandate_id
WHERE t.direction = 'outbound' AND t.kind IN ('intro','owner_approach')
  AND t.occurred_at > now() - interval '90 days'
GROUP BY 1, 2;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_reply_stats ON analytics.reply_stats (template_code, sector_code) NULLS NOT DISTINCT;

-- Refresh every 10 minutes without blocking readers (needs the unique indexes above).
SELECT cron.schedule('refresh-analytics', '*/10 * * * *', $$
  REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY analytics.pipeline_summary;
  REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY analytics.stage_durations;
  REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY analytics.mandate_funnel;
  REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY analytics.reply_stats;
$$);

These are derived, so they never duplicate a fact: each can be dropped and rebuilt from core, comms, docs and dataroom at any time. A new report adds a view here, not a column on a working table.

Before vs after

"Before" is wusool-infra as it runs on dev today. "After" is the finished system once phase 8 ships, as the Plan and Database tabs describe it. Each drawing names the module that owns each part.

Components and data flow

Before

Slack is the main way in, Attio holds the record, and Postgres is a copy kept current by the webhook and a nightly resync. Slow work runs as in-process tasks, so a deploy or crash loses whatever was running.

After: structure

Twenty-eight modules in five layers, each owning its own tables. Every write passes through the event engine and puts a message on attio_outbox in the same transaction, so Attio is updated after Postgres, not before. Sign-in moves out of matching_engine into identity, and organizations folds into crm. Mail and calendar arrive through google_workspace and the existing interactions module (PR #396), which owns the comms schema; there is no separate comms module, and no Google sign-in for users, who sign in with Slack.

After: data flow through the queues

Each row is one queue: the component that puts a message on it, the worker that takes it off, and where the result lands. Before, none of this had a queue; the closest thing was an in-process task.

Write path

Before, a save writes Attio and then Postgres as two separate calls, so a failure between them leaves the two out of step until the webhook or the nightly resync catches up. After, the record, its event and the outbox message commit together; if Attio is down, the message waits on the queue and is retried.

Data model

Before

A deal row points at one buyer company and one seller company, and its progress lives in counters such as nda_count and responses. There is no row per buyer being worked on a deal, so there is nothing to hang a status, a next step or an email on.

After

The counterparty is the new centre: one row per buyer (or target) on a mandate or a search list, always pointing at a buyer or seller role. Status history, touchpoints, drafts, offers and data room links all hang off it, which is what lets the Buyers tab and the funnel count real rows instead of counters. The full table list is in the Database guide and DDL tabs.

Why counterparties: Attio today versus the new setup

Attio's deal record (Deal_V2) holds one buyer_id, one seller_id and one deal_stage. The stage options mix two different things: the client engagement (Inbound, Qualified, Mandate Signed, Teaser Distributed) and one buyer's progress (NDA Circulated, NDA Signed, LOI Received, Passed). Progress across many buyers is kept in hand-typed counters: nda_count, tier1_contacted, responses, counterparty_interested, universe_size and shortlist_size. Attio has nowhere to put one buyer's progress on a deal.

Example. A nursery group wants to sell, and Jules works 40 possible buyers. The company names below are illustrative.

In Attio, option A: one deal record for the mandate.

FieldValue
seller_idthe nursery group
buyer_idempty, or whichever buyer is furthest along
deal_stageNDA Signed, but signed by whom?
tier1_contacted / responses / nda_count40 / 11 / 6
  • Which six signed the NDA? The counters can't say, and because someone types them, they drift from reality.
  • Who passed, and why? There is no field for it.
  • When did we last email buyer 23, and is a follow-up due? There is nowhere to hang an email or a next step for one buyer.
  • How long did buyers sit at teaser sent? There is one stage_changed_at for the whole deal.

In Attio, option B: one deal record per buyer–seller pair.

  • The pipeline is inflated: it shows 40 cards for one client, so deal counts and the funnel are 40 times too high.
  • Deal-level fields are copied 40 times: fee, retainer, advisor, mandate dates and the teaser. Changing the fee means 40 edits, and the copies drift apart.
  • One stage does two jobs: it describes the buyer and the engagement at once, so "Mandate Signed" on buyer 17's record makes no sense.

Today's data uses both patterns. That is why core.counterparties keeps attio_pair_deal_record_id: the migration turns each old pair deal into one counterparty row.

The same mandate in the new setup. One core.mandates row: side sell, the client's seller_role, stage, fee and team, entered once. Then 40 core.counterparties rows, one per buyer, each pointing at that buyer's buyer_role:

BuyerStatusNext stepLast contactNDA signed
Gulf Edu Capitalnda_signedSend CIM, due 14 Nov9 Nov, email6 Nov
Horizon PEpassed, reason: ticket too smallNone2 NovNone
Al Safa GroupcontactedFollow-up 1, due 13 Nov7 NovNone
37 more

What that buys:

  1. Numbers come from the rows. "6 NDAs signed" is a count of rows with nda_signed_on, so it can't drift, and clicking it shows which six.
  2. Each buyer has its own history. counterparty_status_history records when each buyer entered and left each status, which gives time in status and conversion per buyer.
  3. Emails and follow-ups attach to the right buyer. A reply from Horizon PE updates that buyer's Last contact and stops only its own follow-ups.
  4. Pass reasons can be counted. "30% passed on ticket size" becomes a query.
  5. A buyer's details live once. Gulf Edu Capital's criteria sit on its buyer_role; on five mandates, all five rows point at that one role instead of keeping copies.
  6. The deal record only describes the deal. The mandate stage is the client engagement; buyer statuses live on the counterparty rows.
  7. Buy-side works the same way, flipped. One buyer client, with 30 to 50 counterparty rows pointing at the targets' seller_roles.

Each company can appear once per deal (uq_cp_mandate_org), and one mandate is either sell-side or buy-side, never both. While Attio is still in use, core.v_mandate_attio works out the old Deal_V2 counters (NDA count, universe and shortlist size, contacted, responses, interested, time in stage) from these rows, and the outbox writes them to Attio, so nobody types them by hand.
